To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel highly selective polymer electrolyte membrane for the separation of SF6/N2 mixtures was prepared by the incorporation of Cu(NO3)(2) into a POZ matrix.

Cu(NO3) 2 solvated with water in the PO2 membrane was observed to be more highly ordered ionic aggregate than free ions or ionic pairs, and the N2/SO2 selectivity of the composite membrane was increased to 28 with a N2 flux of 11.3 GPU at a PO2 /Cu(NO3)2 ratio of 1 : 0.7.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new polymer electrolyte membrane for the separation of SF6 and other gases.
the development of a novel polymer electrolyte membrane for SF6/N 2 gas separation.
the development of a new type of highly selective polymer electrolyte membrane for SF6/N 2 separation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu(NO3) 2 solvated with water in the POZA matrix was responsible for the increase of the selectivity of the N2/SO2 mixture.

Cu(NO3) 2 solvated with water in POZ has the highest N2/SF 6 selectivity among all the composite membranes tested, which is due to the coordinative interaction of water and Cu2+ ions with F atoms of SF 6.
the N2/S6F selectivity was improved by the coordinative interactions between Cu(NO3) 2 and POZ, and that the N2 permeance was enhanced by the solvation of Cu(NO3).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cu2+ ions in the POZ/Cu2+ membrane were activated by the solvation of water, and the activated Cu2+ ions were involved in the barrier effect for N2/SF gas separation.
the incorporation of Cu(NO3)(2) into the POZ membrane resulted in a highly selective membrane, with a N2/SF(6) selectivity of 28.0 at a POZ:Cu(NO3)2 ratio of 1 :0.7, and a permeance of 1.1 GPU.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N2/SO2 selectivity of Cu(NO3)(2)/POZ membranes was 2.8 times greater than that of Nafion membranes at the same SF6 permeance.
the N2/SO2 selectivity can be increased by the addition of a Cu2+ ion to the polymer electrolyte membrane, and the N2 permeance is also maintained.
the Cu(NO3) 2/POZ composite is a highly promising membrane for SF6/N 2 separation, and that the selectivity of this membrane can be improved further by optimizing the Cu(NO3)/POZ mole ratio.
